state.misconception_label: Ignores negative sign when expanding bracket

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: John is expanding these three brackets: \( (x+5)(x-3)(x+6) \) He finds it helpful to split the first bracket and view the problem as follows: \( x(x-3)(x+6)+5(x-3)(x+6) \) He expands the brackets further. Before he simplifies, what are the terms than contain an \( \boldsymbol{x}^{2} \) ? I got \( \begin{array}{l}+6 x^{2} \\ +3 x^{2} \\ +5 x^{2}\end{array} \) because I forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think you forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive in this case? Can you think of a way to approach the problem that might help you remember that rule next time?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I just got mixed up because I was focusing on the numbers too much and didn't really think about the signs. Maybe I should write out the signs more clearly when I expand the brackets? But I'm still a bit confused about how to keep track of them all. Can you show me a step-by-step way to do it?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of a way to visually represent the signs when expanding the brackets? Perhaps using different colors for positive and negative terms could help you keep track of them more easily. Let's try working through an example together step by step to see if that approach helps clarify things for you.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: That sounds like a good idea! I think using different colors might help me see which terms are positive and which are negative. Can we try that with the example? I'm still not sure how to keep track of everything when I expand the brackets, especially with the signs.
